newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poland needs more grain after flood-French attache.
newsitem.headline: Poland needs more grain after flood-French attache.

text.p: Poland is likely to increase its grain imports this season in the wake of recent flooding, France's agricultural attache to Warsaw said on Wednesday.

Attache Jean Gault told Reuters he expected overall grain losses of almost a million tonnes and rapeseed losses of between 200,000 and 300,000 tonnes after the flooding in southern and western Poland in past weeks.
He did not give a precise import figure but said that imports mainly of wheat could rise above last season's levels.
The International Grains Council on July 3 estimated Poland's 1997/98 (July/June) soft wheat imports at 500,000 tonnes, well down from last season's 1.8 million.
"There will be more imports than in 1996," Gault said, however. "With almost a million tonnes of losses, we can assume that the imports will be rising."
He expected the imports to focus on high-quality wheat for blending with local grades.
Before the floods, Poland's cereals crop was heading towards 23.8 to 24 million tonnes, he said. But farmers' hopes of a normal crop had been overtaken by the weather.
The grain crop is also expected to suffer some quality problems, while the country's grain stocks of some four million tonnes are already generally of mediocre quality, he said.
A senior Polish analyst said on Tuesday flooding had covered as much as 140,000 hectares of grain fields but that there was too little information to estimate crop losses yet.
Local analysts have estimated the crop at the lower end of a forecast range between 23.6 and 24.7 million tonnes.
Hamburg-based oilseed letter Oil World has said Poland's rapeseed crop could fall to 350,000 tonnes from 461,000 tonnes last year.-
